Domestic Workers

The Supreme Court directed Union Government to enact comprehensive law to stipulate the rights of domestic workers and set up a committee for framework on this. Even the court directed to submit the committee report in 6 months but in vain.

India has 40 million to 90 million domestic workers, majority of them are women and girls. Most of them are SC, ST. These workers may face harassment, abuse etc. Child labour is rampant.

Domestic workers may be:

1. live-in workers residing in employer's home

2. Live – out workers commuting daily.

Exploitative Employment Agencies and Brokers

Many domestic workers are migrant workers even from neighbouring countries, not only from another state.

Their contribution to global economy is recognised by the International Labour Organisation (ILO), hence passed Convention in 2011 to ensure the rights and protections of domestic workers.

While India voted in favour of this, it is yet to ratify it.

Interestingly, multiple attempts to pass such legislations since 1950.

The National Platform for Domestic Workers formed in 2012. It drafted Domestic Workers (Regulation of Work and Social Security) Bill in 2017.

State-Level Initiatives

Tamil Nadu Govt set up welfare board under Tamil Nadu Manual Workers Act, 1982.

Under this, minimum wage of 39 Rupees per hour.

Karnataka Govt announced introduction of Domestic Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Bill, 2025.

In India only 12 states stipulate minimum wage for domestic workers.

Examples: Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala, Telangana etc.

→ All South India states

Legal Framework

  • Unorganised Workers Social Security Act, 2008
  • Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition, Redressal) Act, 2013
  • ILO Convention (189) – 2011 – yet to be ratified
  • Minimum Wages Act, 1948

  • Self Employed Women's Association
  • All India Domestic Workers Union
